label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Tolu, na me you are looking for 😭 Biology 100L, wanted Medicine and Surgery. I scored 251 in JAMB 2025 and got Biology in a federal uni here in Lagos. So I won’t tell you “just accept” or “just rewrite” like the decision is easy. I’m inside it now and even me, I’m still figuring some things out.

First, sorry about how you’re feeling. The day I saw Biology on my portal, I locked myself inside my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t eat. You know when you’ve already pictured yourself studying a particular course, then the portal just shows you something else? It wasn’t even that I knew anything bad about Biology. It was just not what I had planned for myself.

My mum was still telling people in church that I was doing Medicine for like two months after that. I had to actually beg her to stop. So if part of what is paining you is how to explain it to people, or feeling like you’ve disappointed your family, I understand that part too. But please don’t let embarrassment choose your next step for you.

Let me answer the transfer question properly, because that was one of the first things I wanted to know too.

**Transfer to Medicine is real, but it is NOT automatic.** What our level adviser told us is that you need a CGPA of at least **4.5 out of 5**, AND there must be space in Medicine. Those are two separate things. Getting the grades doesn’t mean they must take you if there’s no space.

According to her, about six people got moved into Medicine from the whole faculty last year. She thinks over 40 applied. I wasn’t there counting applicants myself, so I’m telling you exactly where I got that information from, not presenting it as something I personally verified. But even from that, you can see why “enter Biology and just read hard” is not the full gist.

She also told us that you need to meet the Medicine cut-offs for JAMB and post-UTME too. So your 268 alone doesn’t settle whether you qualify for transfer. I don’t know your school’s cut-offs or what you scored in post-UTME. You need to check both, and ask how they apply those requirements to transfer applicants in your own school.

That’s why I don’t agree with Kingsley saying transfer is a myth. It happens. But favour’s “just read hard” also makes it sound simpler than it is. Reading hard is important, obviously, but there are requirements and available spaces involved. Somebody’s neighbour doing it doesn’t mean everybody who tries will get it.

And let me not come here and form academic weapon for you: **my own first-semester CGPA is 4.31.** Not 4.5. I’m still trying. Before entering, it’s very easy to say, “I’ll just get 4.5 and transfer.” When you start doing the courses and writing the exams, you’ll understand that the “just” is doing plenty work in that sentence 😭

For our 100L, we do BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. It’s not only Biology from morning till night. Physics and maths are the ones dealing with people here. So if you accept, please come ready to work across the courses, not only the ones you like or feel are connected to Medicine.

Also, small practical things people don’t always mention: my lab coat was ₦6,500, dissecting kit was ₦9,000, and practical manual was extra. Those are my own costs, not a price list for your school, but ask about those things too so you and your parents know what you’re preparing for.

Now, is Biology bad? Honestly, no. I’m enjoying parts of it much more than I expected, especially genetics and cell biology.

Our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted. Me that had cried over getting Biology, I was fine 😂 I was interested in what we were doing. That was the day I first thought, “Wait, I actually like this thing.”

It didn’t suddenly erase my original plan. I didn’t leave the lab and announce that I never wanted Medicine again. But it helped me separate “this wasn’t my first choice” from “this course is bad.” Those two things are not the same, and I had been treating them like they were.

You might enter and discover parts you genuinely enjoy too. But I can’t promise that you will, and liking Biology is not the same thing as getting the medical training you originally wanted. So I wouldn’t advise you to accept it purely as a waiting room for MBBS.

The question I think you should ask yourself is: **if the transfer doesn’t happen, would I be willing to continue studying Biology?** Not “will I be excited about it immediately?” You’re disappointed now, so that might be asking too much. But could you see yourself giving the course a fair chance? If the answer is a definite no, that matters. Don’t ignore it because somebody has assured your dad that transfer is easy.

On rewriting, I won’t tell you it’s wrong either. If Medicine is truly what you want and you’re ready to prepare again, rewriting is a valid option. Just don’t let anybody sell you a guaranteed outcome there too.

My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected Pharmacy because she wanted Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and she’s still at home. I’m not mentioning her to frighten you or say she made a foolish decision. I’m saying that “one year is nothing, just rewrite” can sound very light from somebody who isn’t the one living through the uncertainty. Sometimes it doesn’t end up being only one year.

Staying home isn’t as easy as people make it sound. But that also doesn’t mean you should accept a course you know you don’t want just because your mates are entering school. Neither decision should be made only out of fear.

Before that acceptance deadline, please go to your own faculty or department and ask for the exact transfer rules. Ask about the CGPA, JAMB and post-UTME requirements, whether Biology students can apply, and how available spaces affect selection. If they have the rules written down, ask to see them. You and your dad need the actual conditions, not just “people normally transfer.”

Please don’t trust forum people alone, including me. I’m sharing what our adviser told us and what my experience has been. Your school’s rules are what will affect you.

And one more thing, ask yourself quietly whether you want to study and practise Medicine, or whether some of the pressure is wanting to be “Doctor” for your parents. I’m not saying you don’t genuinely want it. I just know that family expectations can become so loud that it’s hard to hear your own mind. You can love your parents and still be honest with yourself about whose dream you’re chasing.

My own advice is to get the facts from your school first, then decide with both possible outcomes in mind. If you accept Biology, know that transfer may not happen. If you rewrite, know that Medicine next time is not guaranteed either. Which uncertainty are you more willing and prepared to deal with?

You’re allowed to cry over this. I did plenty. Just try not to make the whole decision while you’re still in that first shock. Biology is not a punishment, and rewriting is not a failure. Whatever you choose, this admission outcome is not the end of your world, even if it feels very big right now. ❤️
